description: Trade based on deep orderbook layering (levels 3-5 vs 1-2 net bid-ask ratio) filtered to uncertain markets (mid 0.40-0.60). Uses first snapshot in market window. net_deep signal: 1686 trades, 51.5% WR, $0.085/trade. All other imbalance signals (total, L1, weighted) were negative. Statistical test: z=0.59, p=0.28 — NOT significant vs baseline.
hypothesis: In lopsided markets, orderbook shape is mechanically skewed by price level. Restricting to uncertain markets (mid 0.40-0.60) should isolate the informational component of MM layering from the mechanical component.
next_steps: net_deep shows slight positive PnL ($0.085/trade) but is NOT statistically significant (p=0.28, z=0.59). The 0.7% WR edge over baseline is consistent with noise. Total/L1/weighted imbalance signals all lost money (~48.9% WR). The hypothesis that uncertainty filtering isolates informational MM layering is not supported — the signal is too weak. Most 5m BTC markets have well-populated 5-level books at open, but the layering pattern carries negligible directional information. Not worth pursuing further as a standalone signal.
